reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: src/edit.rs manages the selected IFILE together with ch input state, ordinary descriptors, alternate FILE pipes and allocated alternate names. edit_ifile stages candidate resource values before replacing curr_ifile.
owner_creation.invariant: Selected-file identity and each native resource need separate lifetimes.
limitations: The raw IFILE handle is not a Rust-owned aggregate of all these resources.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/edit.rs borrows filename/alternate-name pointers from IFILE and retains saved handles across switching. save_curr_ifile increments a hold counter; reedit releases it before trying saved/neighbor entries.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A saved handle must remain valid through reopen or fallback selection.
limitations: A hold count alone does not encode every raw alias retirement rule.

callback_targets.analysis: src/edit.rs uses direct open/pipe/modeline/history calls; terminate can reach edit(NULL) through quit. The latter dispatches edit_ifile(NULL), which closes the currently selected file.
callback_targets.invariant: Cleanup entry must not overlap an active file-owner mutation.
limitations: The source-traced asynchronous cleanup route remains M0-SIG-003.

invalidation.analysis: src/edit.rs close_file obtains screen position before ch_close, closes alternate input and nulls alternate filename/curr_ifile. Later activation clears positions, line numbers and highlights for the selected file.
invalidation.invariant: File replacement must invalidate every associated navigation/render alias.
limitations: The sequence depends on coordinated cross-module raw state.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/edit.rs closes the old selected owner before assigning the new curr_ifile and calling ch_init/check_modelines. The switch is a sequence of shared writes and resource calls rather than one reversible aggregate commit.
mutation_commit.invariant: Candidate and old resource ownership must be identifiable at each switch step.
limitations: This review does not prove rollback of every post-activation operation.

release_pair.analysis: src/edit.rs close_pipe uses pclose for a FILE stream and frees only its allocated error message; close_altpipe clears its stored alias afterward. close_file delegates ordinary input release to ch_close.
release_pair.invariant: A FILE stream must use its process-stream counterpart, not a bare descriptor free.
limitations: Retained-input flags still affect whether an alternate pipe is closed.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/edit.rs handles a failed saved-file reopen by trying neighbors and eventually quit; close_pipe diagnoses pclose failure but has already consumed the stream. Errors cannot be described as leaving all original owners intact.
error_cleanup.invariant: Error paths must distinguish a consumed resource from a reusable handle.
limitations: No global primary-error and rollback proof is inferred from local diagnostics.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/edit.rs is directly reachable from terminate -> quit -> edit(NULL); close_file then reads position and invokes cache/alternate-input cleanup. M0-SIG-003 and M0-MEM-001 remain open for reentrant owner coordination.
signals_handoff.invariant: Asynchronous quit must not retire owners borrowed by suspended operations.
limitations: This packet records the route without independently executing it.

src/signal.rs.relationship: terminate at src/signal.rs:83-85 enters quit without deferring cleanup; edit.rs is reached from that asynchronous owner-retirement path.

src/pager.rs.relationship: quit calls edit(NULL) at src/pager.rs:967-970, establishing the external entry into edit_ifile(NULL) and close_file rather than a speculative editor reentry.
